title: Run complete manual-payment lifecycle and Admin browser acceptance
verify: Real compiled Medusa/PostgreSQL runtime creates or reuses one FT-007 pending order with an unpaid native system payment collection, and Admin proves paid/processing/completed/refunded behavior.
The browser/Admin flow shows contacts, products, delivery data, payment method/status, order status, total, and logical checkout_state on the built-in Admin order detail.

Admin cancellation of an unpaid order leaves it in the database as canceled, removes it from the active customer cart, releases the existing reservation through the supported path, and rejects a late payment event.

Reservation state remains held after Admin marks payment paid and is consumed only through native fulfillment; duplicate/contradictory event paths produce no duplicate order, reservation, stock, or lifecycle mutation, and no provider request is made.
Artifacts are privacy-safe, processes/ports/fixtures are cleaned up, and T3 verification records semantic-pass, HUMAN_CHECKPOINT: done, and ROLLBACK_RECOVERY_NOTE: present.
evidence_required: Backend runtime report for lifecycle transitions, native payment/fulfillment status, reservation consumption, terminal guards, and no duplicate mutation.
Browser/Admin report or trace for all required operator fields and lifecycle states using synthetic content.
Privacy scan, cleanup/process report, typecheck/build/lint output, and complete T3 functional/semantic/checkpoint/recovery evidence.
constraints: Use the real local Medusa/PostgreSQL/backend/storefront/Admin boundaries and existing synthetic auth/runtime harnesses.
Use only the native Admin mark-as-paid action over the unpaid system collection; do not call YooKassa, simulate a provider handoff, or add provider credentials.
Evidence must exclude real PII, production data, secrets, cookies, bearer values, OAuth tokens, session IDs, and raw provider payloads.
Do not add a custom Admin replacement, direct database browser route, parallel order store, or inventory ledger.
invariants: Admin-visible fields remain truthful across lifecycle transitions.
Payment confirmation and every order-status change are native Admin-authoritative and never Store/browser-authoritative.
Native reservations and inventory changes are observed at the supported fulfillment boundary.
Cleanup and repeated runs are isolated, deterministic, and recoverable.
purpose: Prove the complete FT-008 lifecycle and operator surface through the real local runtime and built-in Admin browser flow.
success_outcome: A sanitized backend/browser run demonstrates correct lifecycle state, reservation/inventory behavior, required Admin fields, and safe duplicate/terminal handling.
anti_goals: Do not use live payment/provider mutation or production data.
Do not alter feature source to satisfy a report-only assertion or hide a native Admin mismatch.
Do not implement FT-009 return/webhook UI or FT-010 email behavior.

forbidden_scope: YooKassa live calls, credentials, webhook transport, return-page authority
production data, secrets, cookies, tokens, direct database browser access
stop_conditions: The real Admin/browser boundary cannot be exercised with an existing local synthetic operator setup.
Evidence cannot prove native reservation consumption and no duplicate/terminal mutation.
Acceptance requires a new production auth/bearer mechanism or live provider credentials.
A discovered implementation defect requires edits outside the scoped lifecycle/Admin acceptance files.
